title: A finite locally free quotient admits a local section
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $0\to\mathcal E_1\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal E_2\xrightarrow{q}\mathcal E_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal E_3$ locally free of constant finite rank in the sense of [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. For every point $x\in X$ there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ and an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $s:\mathcal E_3|_U\to\mathcal E_2|_U$ such that $q|_U\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal E_3|_U}$.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: local splitting

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. By [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], choose a Zariski open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$, a finite rank $d\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_V$-linear isomorphism $t:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal E_3|_V$. Let $e_i=t(\mathbf e_i)\in\mathcal E_3(V)$ for $1\le i\le d$, where $\mathbf e_i$ is the $i$th standard basis section.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: 'locally the sequence splits'; choose a trivialization of the quotient

proof.text: Exactness at $\mathcal E_3$ makes $q$ an epimorphism [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. For each $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1) to $q|_V$ and $e_i$: an open cover of $V$ carries local lifts of $e_i$. Choose a member $V_i$ containing $x$ and a section $b_i\in\mathcal E_2(V_i)$ with $q(b_i)=e_i|_{V_i}$. Since $d$ is finite, $U=V\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^d V_i$ is open and contains $x$; each $b_i|_U$ lifts $e_i|_U$. When $d=0$, take $U=V$ and there are no lifts to choose.

source.place: Section Tag 01AF (section-kernels), cokernel and local surjectivity; Lemma Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian), exactness of sheaves of modules

proof.text: On $U$, define $s$ by $s(\sum_{i=1}^d a_i e_i|_W)=\sum_{i=1}^d a_i b_i|_W$ for every open $W\subseteq U$ and $a_i\in\mathcal O_X(W)$. The basis from step 1 makes the coefficients unique; this formula is $\mathcal O_W$-linear and commutes with restrictions, so it gives an $\mathcal O_U$-module morphism. Applying $q$ gives $q(s(\sum_i a_i e_i))=\sum_i a_i q(b_i)=\sum_i a_i e_i$, hence $q|_U\circ s=\mathrm{id}$. For $d=0$, both $\mathcal E_3|_U$ and the sum are zero and the same identity holds.
